title: Henriette de Clèves and Renato Birago to the duke of Nevers, Lyon, September 1574, BnF fr. 3315 ff. 15-16, 21

steps.what: Mapped manuscript folios to Gallica openings and fetched full-resolution images of ff. 15 and 21 and the neighbouring keys.
Found and transcribed the complete clear Italian fair copy beneath Birago's cipher flap at f. 21.
Identified the small writing between the cipher lines of f. 15 as a contemporary word-by-word decipherment, not random pen trials.
Fetched Nevers no. 2 of 1584 from BnF fr. 3995 f. 16 and confirmed that it is only a sibling key, not the exact target alphabet.
Checked a superficially similar Henri III appeal printed by Lavisse and rejected it as a crib because it predates this letter and has a different sender.
Read the opening on f. 15 and the clear ending on f. 16r; continuous transcription of the cipher leaves remained blocked by the overwritten minute hand.

outcome.fraction_read_source: f. 21 is complete (271 whitespace-delimited words in the transcribed quotation); the f. 15 opening and f. 16 clear ending are legible, but most of the two dense cipher pages are not continuously transcribed. The 0.4 is a rough page-and-text-weighted estimate, not a token count.
outcome.notes: The target is not wholly undecrypted: both leaves preserve their own reading aids. f. 21 is complete; f. 15 remains palaeographically incomplete.

gaps.detail: Minute interlinear French is crossed by larger cipher signs and locally faded; enlarged crop pass recovered anchors but not a defensible continuous text.
1584 Nevers no. 2 is similar but differs. Exact table could be rebuilt by glyph-level alignment of the f. 21 cipher slip with its interlinear Italian gloss.
Fair copy appears to read 'per saluato suo'; perhaps a personal name or abbreviation.

prior.where: The manuscript itself preserves a contemporary interlinear decipherment on f. 15, a clear ending on f. 16r, and a complete clear copy under the cipher flap on f. 21; Tomokiyo described the system but published no reading.

human: The human selected the target and requested a solve/read followed by a write-up. No target-specific transcription or cryptanalytic intervention.
